sources.title: Human History Map, Islamic and Hindu states: index and decoded outlines
sources.note: Own-project factual-data exception. Exact ID islamic-and-hindu-states, 1530-1700; world 1530 has a main polygon and a small Konkan coastal polygon, world 1600 repeats the broad main outline, world 1650 contracts to east-central India. Ramnagar, Jabalpur, Nagpur, Raipur, Ratanpur and Bastar inside main outlines; Ahmedabad and Gaur only in early outlines. All target IDs remained distinct.

sources.title: Jitu Mishra, Gujarat Sultanate: Architecture, e-PG Pathshala
sources.note: Original institutional teaching module read, printed pages2 and5: Gujarat annexation 1573. Other compressed or problematic earlier chronology excluded; no broad characterizations of religions adopted.

sources.title: Banglapedia, Rajmahal, The battle of
sources.note: Original Bangladesh Asiatic Society encyclopedia indexed text checked: fall of Husain Shahi 1538 and Daud Karrani defeated 1576. Direct page sometimes returns empty; reproducible query site:en.banglapedia.org Rajmahal 1576 Daud. No implication all regional resistance ended at once.

sources.title: NCERT, Our Pasts II, Tribes, Nomads and Settled Communities
sources.note: Original PDF directly read, printed53,55-57: Banjaras and Peter Mundy, Gond administration and elephant trade, later survival. Its 1565 Durgavati date is not adopted; independent university and scholarly sources give 1564. Runtime NCERT works are different titles (Themes in Indian History II; Politics in India since Independence), not this book.

sources.title: Rani Durgavati Vishwavidyalaya, About Rani Durgavati
sources.note: Original university biography read: Dalpat marriage, widow regency, ministers Adhar Kayastha and Man Thakur, invasion and death24June 1564. Unneeded disputed birth/genealogy, death of husband and Malwa chronology excluded.

sources.title: K. G. Vyas, Water management in the times of Gonds of Central India (2022)
sources.note: Direct first-person expert geological/hydrological synthesis, author former Drinking Water Mission consultant. Chain of five tanks and step-well aquifer construction read; domestic-function inference clearly attributed. Excluded unsupported universal adequacy, no failures in500years, exact medieval rainfall and tank-by-tank construction dates.

sources.title: Permanent Delegation of India to UNESCO, The Gond monuments of Ramnagar, Mandla (2024 submission)
sources.note: Direct state-party tentative-list submission, not a World Heritage inscription or UNESCO certification. Used physical Moti Mahal drainage/rooms and minister residence privacy/shade. Capital move dated 1657 here versus 1667 in Dixit; card gives seventeenth century without picking disputed year. Long royal genealogy not treated as proven early history.

sources.title: Amulya Dixit and Tanashree Redij, Ramnagar Inscription: Making of the Temple and the Queen (2023)
sources.note: Original scholarly PDF read. Printed32-33: RI42 and exact transliteration/translation; RI45 ponds/gardens; RI51 scholars; RI52 named architects; discussion dates inscription 1667. Scholarly edition depends on earlier readings of damaged inscription. Sample kept in published Roman transliteration; no reconstructed Devanagari. Royal praise distinguished from observed living conditions.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Bridal casket, 2024.480a,b
sources.note: Direct museum catalogue: Gujarat and Goa or Lisbon, second half16th century, teak/mother-of-pearl/silver, Indian technique and European form, Portuguese clients primarily in Asia. Composite place attribution retained; not a typical Gujarati dowry asserted.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Mother-of-Pearl: A Tradition in Asian Lacquer, pen box entry (2006)
sources.note: Original curatorial exhibition text read; LACMA M73.5.340 early17th-century Gujarat pen box, Persian verses about calligraphy, shell/mastic export and domestic production. Broad claim that all young men/women were expected to be calligraphers not generalized; no unverified verse copied.

proposedOverrides.name: Islamic and Hindu states of South Asia
proposedOverrides.summary: A changing South Asian atlas umbrella, with regional examples from Gujarat, Bengal and central Indian Gond kingdoms, rather than a single religious or political union.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Standalone changing atlas umbrella; no aliases
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Four decoded features across 1530,1600,1650. Earlier main outline includes Gujarat/Bengal; later outline excludes them and covers east-centralIndia. Ramnagar point80.5084,22.6115 inside every main outline. Tiny1530 Konkan coastal patch is acknowledged without guessing a dynasty.
batchIdentityNotes.boundaries: Separate from minor-states (Anatolia/Armenia200-1BCE), minor-states-under-indian-influence (SoutheastAsia600-800), other Hindu-state umbrellas and every named polity. No unified religious society inferred.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Gujarat 1573 and Bengal 1576 political changes precede repeated1600 polygon. Capital move Ramnagar has conflicting 1657/1667 reports; only inscription securely dated 1667, palace described17thcentury.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No securely localized ordinary-house medical protocol or toilet installation established here. Water infrastructure, family caravans, court learning and crafts are concrete evidence with limits. Elite objects and buildings not generalized to all households.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Sanskrit in Devanagari,1667 Ramnagar; shown in published Roman transliteration from damaged inscription, not Gondi language or invented original letterforms.
